# Error-Handling Requirements Quality Checklist: Stop Generation Button

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality review of failure, race, and degradation requirements for the stop feature — tests whether the requirements are complete, unambiguous, and measurable, NOT whether the implementation works.
**Created**: 2026-10-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [plan.md](../plan.md) · [contracts/stop-generation.md](../contracts/stop-generation.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Failure Scenario Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are requirements defined for stop behavior when the backend halt call fails at the transport level (unreachable route, network refusal), beyond the generic "momentarily unavailable" clause? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK002 Is the path where the generation identifier never arrives (no task id in the stream) specified as a distinct failure mode with its own user-visible outcome? [Gap, Spec §FR-006 vs contracts §1]
- [x] CHK003 Are stop requirements defined for demo/fallback mode (no backend configured), or is that scenario's absence from the spec intentional? [Gap — covered only in research R6/plan, not in spec requirements]
- [x] CHK004 Is what the user sees when the halt call fails specified (silent clean stop vs visible warning), so acceptance tests assert one behavior instead of either? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK005 Are input-validation and key-handling requirements for the new stop request documented at the requirements level (constraints on request fields, same-origin assumption, no key exposure)? [Traceability, contracts §2]
- [x] CHK006 Is the acceptable end-state bounded when a halt fails permanently — may the generation run to natural completion server-side, and is that outcome explicitly acceptable? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006]

## Race Condition Requirements

- [x] CHK007 Is the completion race ("stop lands as `done` arrives") specified with a resolvable, testable outcome rather than the current "never a broken one"? [Measurability, Spec §US-3 Scenario 2]
- [x] CHK008 Is the requirement that the second stop activation is a no-op specified precisely enough to test (what state proves the no-op: no finalize, no backend call, no UI change)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [x] CHK009 Are requirements defined for the interaction between user stop and the inactivity watchdog (stop latch at second 119 of a 120 s silence — does the watchdog still fire)? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases + research R3]
- [x] CHK010 Are cross-tab / cross-client requirements addressed or explicitly excluded (the same conversation open in two browser tabs, one generation, stop clicked in one)? [Gap]
- [x] CHK011 Are requirements specified for stop arriving during a long inter-chunk silence (mid-tool research) as distinct from the thinking phase, or is "thinking or streaming" sufficient coverage? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]

## Degradation & Presentation Honesty

- [x] CHK012 Is the distinction between a stopped turn and an error turn specified (presentation, indicators), or could an error UX be mistaken for a stop? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK013 Are the presentation requirements for a reloaded stopped turn explicit (no caption, no sources, partial text intact), rather than implied by the session-only ruling? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK014 Is the requirement that sources arriving before the stop are kept, while none may arrive after, unambiguous about badge rendering at the stop boundary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK015 Is the empty-stop rule (no assistant bubble when nothing arrived) stated as a requirement, not only an assumption? [Traceability, Spec §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK016 Are accessibility requirements for the Stop control defined (keyboard activation, label), or is their deferral to plan-level defaults recorded as a decision? [Gap]

## Recovery & Continuity

- [x] CHK017 Are post-stop continuity requirements complete across all conversation features, or do they enumerate some (follow-up, resume, delete, search, export) and omit others (title promotion, model badge)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK018 Is the stop-then-immediately-resend requirement specified for the backend's perspective (may the halted conversation be re-queried concurrently with the halt)? [Gap]
- [x] CHK019 Is recovery from a stuck-generation state addressed if the visible stop succeeds but the composer never returns to ready (the exact bug the feature supersedes)? [Gap, research R3]
- [x] CHK020 Are requirements defined for what happens to the generation when the page is closed/reloaded mid-stream (is that a stop, an error, or unspecified)? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Measurability & Acceptance of Failure Requirements

- [x] CHK021 Can SC-005 ("no further content after stop") be verified deterministically — is the measurement procedure (fixed delay, text-growth check) specified in the requirements artifacts? [Measurability, SC-005 + quickstart §C]
- [x] CHK022 Is the definition of "acceptance defect" for a failed backend halt operational (which observable makes it a defect vs a tolerated race)? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006]
- [x] CHK023 Is the 1-second stop SLA (SC-001) defined to include or exclude the backend halt call, so the battery measures the right thing? [Ambiguity, SC-001 vs FR-006]

## Dependencies, Assumptions & Consistency

- [x] CHK024 Are spec FR-006's failure semantics and contracts §2's `ok | no-task | 502` outcomes consistent one-to-one (no spec-visible state without a contract verdict, and vice versa)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-006 vs contracts §2]
- [x] CHK025 Is the assumption that the backend offers a cancellation capability validated against the deployed version (research R1 evidence), and recorded as validated rather than assumed? [Assumption, research R1]
- [x] CHK026 Do the error-handling scenarios in quickstart §D trace back to spec requirements one-to-one, or do some matrix rows test behavior the spec never specified? [Consistency, quickstart §D vs spec]

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
